processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Each steel composition was first melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity, before being cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h.
Ingots were hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, before being air-cooled to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled rods were solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching. This is the terminal state of the C-1.5 sample used for tensile, Charpy impact and EBSD/TEM characterization.

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h and water quenching the Fe30Mn11Al1.5C (C-1.5) steel is single-phase austenite (FCC) with uniformly distributed intragranular κ-carbide precipitates; no ferrite (BCC) phase is present in this composition (EBSD), unlike the 0.6%C steel. Austenite grains are coarse and contain abundant annealing twin boundaries; κ-carbides coarsen to the largest size of the C series.

phases_present.morphology: regular rectangular/square shape, confined growth with {011} as the growth plane

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix
precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenite matrix (evidenced by SAED observations)

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

interfaces.slip_behavior: Because the κ-carbides form a coherent interface with the austenite matrix, their strengthening contribution follows a particle shear model rather than an Orowan mechanism; particle shear strengthening is still active for κ-carbides as large as 50 nm. Shear deformation facilitates glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes, weakening work hardening.
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides precipitate and coarsen in the austenite during solution treatment; their size increases with carbon content, reaching ~50 nm for the 1.5%C (C-1.5) steel, the coarsest of the C series.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS tensile machine; two solution-treated specimens tested and data are the average value of two specimens; stress-strain jumps after yielding are due to extensometer removal

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 1(a)/Fig. 2(a): the 1.5C curve peaks near 1200 MPa but fails earliest (around 22% strain).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy impact specimen (55 mm long, 10 × 10 mm cross-section, 2 mm deep V-notch) cut from solution-treated rods with the V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS impact tester with 500 J capacity; average of two specimens

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to a field emission gun scanning electron microscope (SEM, FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground then electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; average grain sizes by linear intercept method with 15° boundary misorientation definition using Channel 5 software
characterization_methods.purpose: determine phase distribution, grain size and twin boundary fraction of the solution-treated sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: Only austenite present at 1.5%C (no BCC/ferrite); austenite grain size 22.4 ± 1.4 μm; twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 50.2%

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) dark-field imaging with SAED
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: operated at 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at 20 V and -20 °C; dark-field images taken along the [001]γ zone axis using a κ-carbide reflection
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize κ-carbide size, distribution, morphology and orientation relationship with austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbides uniformly distributed; measured average diameter ~80 nm (dark-field) / 50 ± 18 nm (Table 3) for 1.5%C; regular rectangular/square shape; orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ

unmapped_findings: For C-1.5 (Fe30Mn11Al1.5C): σ_TS (maximum true stress just before necking, from UTS^a column) = 1343 MPa and fracture strength σ_FS (FRS^a column) = 1875 MPa (Table 2).
Charpy impact energy Akv-40 = 1.5 ± 0.2 J is the lowest impact toughness among all designed low-density steels, recorded for the Fe30Mn11Al1.5C steel (b0028, b0066).

Yield strength increased from 542 MPa (0.6%C) to 1125 MPa (1.5%C) while tensile elongation decreased from ~60% to ~20% with increasing carbon content (b0025); rapid work softening occurred in the 1.5%C steel.
Two different κ-carbide sizes are reported for the 1.5%C steel: ~80 nm average diameter from dark-field TEM (b0044) and 50 ± 18 nm in Table 3 (b0047).
Density of Fe30Mn11Al1.5C: measured 6.56 g/cm³ (Table 1); calculated from Eq. (3) as 6.55 g/cm³ (b0064).
Nominal/measured chemical composition of C-1.5: C 1.52, Mn 29.67, Al 11.21, Fe Bal. (mass%) (Table 1).

The paper's general models — density model ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (Eq. 3) and shear-strengthening model σ_shear = α f^1/2 d_Car^1/2 (Eq. 4), with yield-strength fit R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5 (MPa/nm^1/2) — are series-wide and not specific to the C-1.5 sample.
